topic: Type Aliases and Compound Types Leading to Surprising Const Behavior
explanation: In advanced C programming, using type aliases (via typedef or using macros) to define compound types can introduce subtle pitfalls, especially when combined with const qualifiers. These aliases may obscure the actual underlying type, leading to unexpected behavior or const correctness issues. Understanding how type aliases interact with const qualifiers and pointer types is crucial for writing correct, maintainable, and bug-free code in complex systems.
keywords: typedef const pitfall, const type alias, typedef const pointer
